posts.subject: Legion Pro 27UD-10 aggressive ABL behavior
posts.author: exhale33
posts.message_html:
Hello everybody. I recently purchased the Legion Pro 27ud-10 monitor and it seems there are some issues with it that i cannot solve (issues that other people have reported, elsewhere over the internet). The most important (and also annoying) one is the aggressive ABL behavior. I have set the monitor to TB400 HDR mode, disabled Dolby Vision and loaded the specific HDR color profile from Lenovo's specific Windows 11 driver (the proper one, from 2025). After a fixed 35 to a maximum of 40 minutes of gaming, ABL kicks in and relegates the monitor's display to very low brightness levels. 

Now this behavior happens regardless of me turning off every option in the OLED Care OSD menu (including Thermal Modulation). If a less bright scene or portion of the game comes up, the ABL is still ON. It does not properly adjust the brightness and i believe this is a firmware issue, most likely the ABL detecting the game as a static image (which obviously, it is not). I tried factory resetting the monitor, same issue. I tried calibrating its display using the Windows HDR Calibration Tool, same behavior. What's even worse, when using the HDR Calibration Tool, the second and third screen (max detail and max full frame luminance) will have me dragging the slider up to 2560 Nits in order for the cross to disappear (which, again, should not be the case, especially in TB400 mode with DV off). 

My questions are: is there any way to fix this? To prevent the (overly) aggressive ABL behavior? Will this monitor receive any firmware updates, with fixes for these issues? Can the monitor even have its firmware upgraded? I am still within the return window and i would like to know if it's worth holding on to a promise or simply returning it and getting a different model (since from what i have read, so far, everyone who's using this is experiencing the same issues as i am).

 

Kind regards!

posts.subject: Re:Legion Pro 27UD-10 aggressive ABL behavior
posts.author: Lorenzo_Lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello guest57610,

Welcome to Lenovo Community

I understand that you are concerned with the ABL behavior on your Legion Pro 27UD-10.
May I know what device are you using with it?
What you’re describing (brightness stepping down after 30 to 40 minutes and not recovering on darker scenes) sounds like protection/limiting engaging under sustained HDR load rather than standard ABL. 
Let’s run through some items to isolate whether this is thermal/driver behavior, tone mapping, or a unit issue.
Key checks and adjustments:
-OSD settings (monitor side)> Ensure HDR Mode is correctly set for your use case. Try toggling between TB400 HDR and the default HDR mode to compare behavior. In OLED Care, confirm any luminance protection features are truly disabled for testing: Logo/Static Protection, Auto Dimming, and Thermal Modulation. Also look for and turn off any “Smart Power”/dynamic brightness features if present. See the user guide. Reboot the monitor after changes. Set Peak Brightness to High/On (if available) and HDR Tone Mapping to Standard/Default.
-Connection and signal path> Test with the bundled/high‑quality cable (Lenovo cable is recommended)  DisplayPort first. If you’re running 4K at very high refresh, temporarily test at 120 Hz in HDR to see if the behavior persists. A lower refresh can reduce sustained panel load and help tell whether thermal limiting is involved. If possible, try HDMI 2.1 at 120 Hz HDR as a comparison. Also test on another PC/GPU if available.
-Windows and GPU driver settings> Update GPU driver to the latest release and Windows to the latest build. Then reinstall the Lenovo monitor driver/ICC from the support page.
-NVIDIA Control Panel/AMD Software: set output to RGB Full, 10‑bpc (if available), and disable any driver‑side dynamic contrast/brightness or “auto tone mapping” features. Avoid third‑party overlays while testing.
-Retry running the Windows HDR Calibration after resetting previous calibration data. If the “max full frame luminance” pattern only clears near extreme values (e.g., ~2560 nits in TB400), that suggests the chain (EDID/tone mapping) isn’t aligning, usually driver or OS side. Try the calibration again after the GPU driver reinstall and with G‑SYNC/FreeSync temporarily off.
-Thermal/usage factors (for diagnosis)> Ensure the rear of the monitor has good airflow, not close to walls or heat sources. As a test, set refresh to 120 Hz and cap in game frame rate for 45 to 60 minutes. If dimming does not occur or is delayed, it points to thermal/power protection. If it still occurs on lighter content immediately after a darker scene, capture a video for support.
-Firmware (when applicable) and monitor drivers are posted on our support site. If no firmware is posted, the unit is running production firmware .
Test, observe and update us how it goes.

Best regards,
Lorenzo_Lenovo

posts.subject: Re:Legion Pro 27UD-10 aggressive ABL behavior
posts.author: exhale33
posts.message_html:
Hello, Lorenzo

 

- I can confirm that all the OLED protection options from the OSD menu are in their "OFF" state (everything except the 5 minute screen refresh which is set to a 6 hours notice). The monitor was rebooted after each individual modification and as a precaution, i even reset it to its factory settings and re-configured it, afterwards; the same pattern occurs regardless of which HDR mode i'm currently using (TB400 or either of the other 3 HDR modes); calibration was properly done on all modes EXCEPT the TB400. I can confirm that the proper Windows 11 driver is installed (after a very long hurdle) and i have since, reinstalled the AMD Adrenaline suite. I can also confirm that the panel is working on its 10-bit mode, 4-4-4 RGB (full). Even with all of the above, doing a calibration while in TB400 mode will allow the slider to be dragged way past 2000nits;

- The cables that i'm using are the ones that came with the monitor's package (supplied by Lenovo); i have tried different DP ports (on both the display as well as my GPU); the GPU is a 7900xtx and i can confirm it working, properly, on a different OLED monitor. I cannot try a different computer/build, this is the only one that's in my household and connecting the monitor to a portable device(smartphone, tablet, etc.) would limit its frame rate throughput (therefore, defeating the purpose of its native 4k@240Hz screen);�

- I have tried recalibrating it in TB400 mode with every syncing technology turned "OFF", same behavior (i can drag the slider way past 2000nits);

- The ambient temperature in the room is around 20 degrees Celsius (rarely going up to 21); there is enough space behind the monitor so airflow is not constricted and there are no heat sources around it; the games that i play are usually capped at 120FPS (since i rarely can achieve a higher number with my aforementioned GPU at 4K resolution) and i can confirm the only games where the frame rate is uncapped are some older, indie titles which are played in SDR mode (all of them have no HDR support);

- I can also confirm that the power delivery to the monitor is done via a professional grade UPS (pure sinewave, active topology); this means that i can monitor the current's flow and since it's connected to my UPS, any possible overcharge due to bad current is avoided and filtered by the UPS;�

- I recently tried to test it in HDR Movie (while gaming) and after 40 minutes (on timer) the brightness was reduced system wide; alt+tabbing would NOT solve it; changing the game's mode from Exclusive Fullscreen to Windowed/Borderless and then back to Exclusive fullscreen would not solve it; keeping the system alt+tabbed while displaying a black background (my current wallpaper) for 5 minutes and then reverting back to the game would NOT solve it;�

I will try to set a screen refresh rate cap of 120Hz and game cap at 60Hz but even if this helps with the described behavior, it also defeats the purpose of the monitor (as i will not be using it in 120Hz mode nor will i game at 60Hz, since i'm not using a console but rather my own desktop PC). I have checked on a daily basis for driver/firmware updates, none are to be found. Even the Windows 11 driver that is listed on the product's homepage is not the right one (i managed to find the correct one by searching through the forums, here and i found someone who shared a link to it; now it is properly recognized in Device Manager). According to LADM, the firmware version is 2.0. If there is a new firmware, somewhere, i have yet to find it or to find if it's even possible to upgrade the monitor's firmware.

 

Kind regards,

Chris T.
